newsitem.title: UK: Allied Domecq aims to improve operations.
newsitem.headline: Allied Domecq aims to improve operations.

text.p: British spirits, pubs and fast food group Allied Domecq sees improving operating performance as the best way forward, having reviewed demerger possibilities, chairman Sir Christopher Hogg said in a statement.
The group saw pretax, pre-exceptional profits for the year slip to 575 million pounds from 645 million pounds previously and paid out a total dividend of 23.59 pence.
Allied Domecq aims to improve operations

The company said that exceptional losses for the year totalled 311 million pounds, including 309 million pounds on the sale of its 50 percent stake in brewer Carlsberg-Tetley for 205 million pounds to Bass in August.
"We are intent on developing the group's two principal businesses to be leaders in their respective industries," Hogg said in the statement.
Allied Domecq said a hefty de-stocking programme in the U.S. had been "the main factor" in a 14 percent fall in spirits and wine trading profits.

But the company said that spirits and wine should see benefits from "our increasing focus on key brand/market combinations, from more favourable shipment patterns and from efficiency gains." ($1=.6069 Pound)
